template.name: Mindray A7 Anaesthetic Machine
template.desc: Class I, one BF applied part (airway hoses, Aux, ACGO, AG+O2). Converted from the CHS Ansur A7 template.

steps.title: Visual inspection
steps.instructions: Inspect the machine, modules, cables and accessories.

items: The case, display screen, buttons, knob, SMR, modules, power cord, wall-mount bracket and accessories have no obvious signs of damage.
The external connecting cables are not frayed and the connector pins are not loose or bent.
The external connectors are not loose and their pins are not bent.
The safety labels and data plate are clearly legible.
The power-on test is passed. The power indicator and alarm system work correctly and the machine starts up properly.

steps.title: Mains voltage
steps.instructions:
Set up for the electrical safety tests:
1. Plug the ESA612 into the mains supply.
2. Connect the anaesthetic machine’s power cord to the ESA612 equipment outlet and switch the machine on.
3. Connect the applied parts (airway hoses, Aux, ACGO, AG+O2) to the ESA612 RA post. They are tested as one type BF applied part; use Change applied parts on the patient leakage step if this machine is different.
Then start the auto sequence. It pauses only when the red test lead has to be moved.

steps.title: Insulation: applied parts to protective earth
steps.instructions: Recorded only. The Ansur template sets no limit for this measurement.

steps.title: Insulation: mains to applied parts
steps.instructions: Must be over 1 Mohm (AS/NZS 3551 B9.3). The Ansur template set no limit for this measurement.

steps.title: Insulation: applied parts to non-earth accessible part
steps.instructions: Clip the red test lead to a conductive, non-earthed accessible part of the machine. Recorded only; the Ansur template sets no limit.

steps.title: Insulation: mains to non-earth accessible part
steps.instructions: Keep the red test lead on the non-earthed accessible part.

steps.title: Enclosure leakage
steps.instructions:
Keep the red test lead on a conductive non-earthed accessible part.
Note: only a representative sample of conductive non-earthed accessible parts needs to be tested.

steps.title: Earth leakage
steps.instructions: Limits: 5000 µA normal, 10000 µA neutral open (AS/NZS 3551:2012+A2 B11.6).

steps.title: System check, manual/auto switch and HFJV test
steps.instructions:
System self-test (Service Manual 6.2):
Refer to the Service Manual (6.2) on how to perform System Self-Test)
6.2.1 System Self-test
1. The system automatically starts a power-on self-test when the machine is started. The system self-test screen is displayed after the power-on self-test is completed. Perform operations as prompted on the main screen.
2. Click Continue to start the self-test.
3. Click Detailed Test Results to view the test result of each test item.
4. Proceed with the operation or troubleshooting based on the test result.
5. The pre-use check screen is displayed after the system self-test is completed. Perform the corresponding pre-use check as prompted.  Upon power-on, the system conducts a self-test to ensure that the alarm system (alarm indicator and speaker) and hardware are functioning properly.  The system self-test includes a leak test and a compliance test to ensure that the relevant hardware, valves, sensors, flowmeters, gas sources, power supply, and modules are functioning properly.  The HFJV test is conducted for the jet branch and safety valve tests to ensure that the relevant hardware, valves, sensors, and power supply are functioning properly.

Manual/auto switch test (6.12.3):
1. Exit the standby mode of the machine.
2. Turn the Auto/Manual switch to the Manual position and confirm that the current mode displayed on the screen is the manual mode.
3. Turn the Auto/Manual switch to the Auto position and confirm that the current mode displayed on the screen is the auto mode.

HFJV test (6.2.3): 1. Power-on: When the time since the last HFJV test exceeds the HFJV test interval, the system automatically starts the power-on self-test after power-on. After the power-on self-test is finished, the system automatically enters the system self-test screen. The system self-test includes the HFJV test. Select the Settings Icon soft key and choose HFJV>HFJV Test Interval to adjust the value of the HFJV test interval. From the main screen: Access the standby screen, select the soft key, and click HFJV Test.
2. Perform operation based on messages on the screen.
3. Perform the corresponding operations according to the test results and help information . To obtain the information, select the Setup soft key and Maintenance soft key on the main interface and select the Information label Log
Mark HFJV N/A if the machine has no HFJV.

items: The unit powers on normally and the power-on test is passed.
AC / battery indicator check.
Battery mode check.
AC mode check.
The unit passes all system checks.
Passes the manual/auto switch test.
HFJV test passes.

steps.title: Auxiliary power receptacles and work light
steps.instructions:
1. Verify that AC voltage always exists on all auxiliary output receptacles, regardless of whether the anesthesia system is enabled or disabled. Use a multimeter to test the voltage and grounding performance of auxiliary output receptacles.
2. Press the work light switch on the right of the primary display once to turn on the work light. Verify that all LED lamps are turned on. Press the switch again (for the second time) and verify that the work light is at high brightness. Press the switch again (for the third time) and verify that the work light is off.

items: Auxiliary power receptacle test.
Work light test.

steps.title: Gas source supply: O2, air and N2O
steps.instructions:
O2: 6.3 Gas Source Supply Test
6.3.1 O2 Source Supply Test Remove the oxygen cylinder from the yoke when performing this test.
1. Connect the machine to the O2 supply interface at the upper wall end by using an oxygen source hose.
2. Check that the oxygen source pressure is in the range of 280 kPa to 600 kPa.
3. Turn on the system switch.
4. Set the O2 flow to 6 L/min (for A5).
5. Open the BFCS door, and fully open the O2 needle valve (for A7).
6. Disconnect the oxygen.
7. Confirm that the Insufficient O2 supply pressure alarm and Low drive gas pressure alarm are generated as the O2 pressure decreases.
8. Check that the monitored value of the O2 source pressure drops to zero.

Air: 6.3.3 Air Source Supply Test Remove the air cylinder from the yoke when performing this test.
1. Connect the machine to the air supply interface at the upper wall end by using an air source hose.
2. Check that the air source pressure is in the range of 280 kPa to 600 kPa.
3. Turn on the system switch.
4. Set the flow control mode to single-branch flow control mode and set the balance gas to air (for A7).
5. Set the ventilation mode to manual.
6. Adjust the air flow to 6 L/min.
7. Disconnect the air source.
8. Check that the air source pressure drops to zero. The air source pressure gauges include a mechanical pressure gauge and an electronic pressure gauge.

N2O: 6.3.2 N2O Source Supply Test Remove the N2O cylinder from the yoke when performing this test.
1. Connect the machine to the N2O supply interface at the upper wall end by using an O2 source hose and a N2O source hose.
2. Check that the pressure of O2 source and N2O source is in the range of 280 kPa to 600 kPa.
3. Turn on the system switch.
4. Set the flow control mode to single-branch flow control mode and set the balance gas to N2O (for A7).
5. Set the ventilation mode to manual.
6. Adjust the N2O flow to 6 L/min.
7. Disconnect the N2O source.
8. Check that the N2O pressure drops to zero.

items: O2: supply pressure is 280–600 kPa.
O2: the system displays "O2 Supply Failure".
O2: the system displays "Drive Gas Pressure Low".
Air: supply pressure is 280–600 kPa.
Air: the system displays "Balance Gas Branch Flow not Achieved".
N2O: supply pressure is 280–600 kPa.
N2O: the system displays "N2O Supply Failure".

steps.title: BFCS: switching, needle valve and flow accuracy
steps.instructions:
Checking the Function of Switching Between EFCS and BFCS
1. When the system is powered on, open the BFCS door in the EFCS state. In the popup window, click Yes. Ensure that the Backup Flow Control is enabled alarm is reported. The backlight of the backup flowmeter should be on.
2. Click Disable Backup Flow Control in the lower left corner of the screen. In the popup window, click Yes and close the BFCS door when the needle valve is turned off. The BFCS door should not be automatically opened. After the BFCS door is closed, the backlight of the backup flowmeter is turned off.
Checking Needle Valve Correspondence Perform the following check when the BFCS is enabled:
1. Confirm that the flow value displayed on the glass tube flowmeter and the main screen is about 1 L/min.
2. Rotate the O2 needle valve and confirm that the flow of the total flowmeter increases with the rotation of the O2 needle valve and can rise to about 15 L/min.
3. Turn off the O2 needle valve. The flow should decrease to about 1 L/min (that is, only the basal flow is reserved).
Checking the Needle Valve Sensitive Switch Open the BFCS door, rotate the O2 needle value for about 1/2 turn from the closed state, and click Disable Backup Flow Control. Make sure that Backup flowmeter must be turned off is displayed and the BFCS door is automatically opened again upon closing. Turn off the O2 needle valve and click Disable Backup Flow Control.The BFCS door can be normally closed.

Basic Flow Test Under BFCS
1. Connect the O2 source input or open the backup O2 cylinder.
2. Enable the BFCS.
3. Verify that the float of the total flowmeter is around 1 L/min. The gas to be tested must be O2 and the O2 needle valve must be adjusted to the minimum value.
Accuracy Verification Test
1. Connect the O2 source.
2. Turn the Auto/Manual switch to Manual and turn the APL valve to SP.
3. Connect the Y-shaped head in the respiratory circuit to the leakage test end and connect the other two ends to the expiratory end and inspiratory end of the circuit.
4. Turn on the backup flow control valve and the backup flowmeter.
5. Adjust the oxygen knob of the backup flowmeter according to the following table and confirm that the total backup flow displayed on the left of the display screen and the reading of the glass tube flowmeter meet the following requirements: Adjust the backup flowmeter Reading of the glass tube flowmeterThe flow is displayed on the left the display Adjust the oxygen knob of the backup flowmeter 2 L/min 1.8 L/min to 2.2 L/min15 L/min 13.5 L/min to 16.5 L/ min

items: The "Backup Flow Control is enabled" alarm is reported and the backup flowmeter backlight is on.
The flow shown on the glass tube flowmeter and the main screen is about 1 L/min.
The total flowmeter flow increases with the O2 needle valve and can rise to about 15 L/min.
"Backup flowmeter must be turned off" is displayed and the BFCS door opens again on closing when the O2 needle valve is about 1/2 turn open.
Backup flowmeter set to 2 L/min: glass tube and screen read 1.8–2.2 L/min.
Backup flowmeter set to 15 L/min: glass tube and screen read 13.5–16.5 L/min.

steps.title: Cylinder supply: O2, air and N2O
steps.instructions:
Mark N/A for cylinders not fitted.

O2: 6.4 Cylinder Supply Test
6.4.1 O2 Cylinder Supply Test
1. Remove the O2 supply hose from the gas inlet assembly.
2. Mount the backup cylinder full of O2 on the backup cylinder yoke.
3. Observe the reading on the O2 high pressure gauge for the entire system. Ensure that the difference between the pressure displayed on the system-based O2 high pressure gauge and the pressure displayed on the cylinder pressure gauge does not exceed 4% of the full-scale reading + 8% of the actual reading.
4. Turn on the system switch and set the ventilation mode to manual.
5. Adjust the O2 flow gradually. The reading of the flowmeter should fluctuate with the set O2 value (for A5).
6. Start BFCS. The system has about 1 L/min basal flow. Adjust the O2 needle valve. The value on the backup flowmeter should fluctuate with the set needle valve (for A7).
7. Turn off the O2 needle valve or BFCS. The machine enters the standby mode. Close the O2 cylinder.
8. Ensure that the pressure value displayed on the system-based O2 high pressure gauge decreases by less than 10% within one minute.
9. Exit and set the O2 flow to 6 L/min.
10.Confirm that the Insufficient O2 supply pressure alarm and Low driving gas pressure alarm are generated as the oxygen source pressure decreases.
11.Check that the reading of the O2 high pressure gauge drops to zero. The drive gas pressure low alarm will occur only when the machine is configured for O2 drive.

Air: 6.4.2 Air Cylinder Supply Test
1. Remove the air source hose from the gas inlet assembly.
2. Mount the backup cylinder full of air on the backup cylinder yoke
3. Observe the reading on the air high pressure gauge for the entire system. Ensure that the difference between the pressure displayed on the system-based air high pressure gauge and the pressure displayed on the cylinder pressure gauge does not exceed 4% of the full-scale reading + 8% of the actual reading.
4. Turn on the system switch and set the ventilation mode to manual.
5. Adjust the air flow gradually. The reading of the flowmeter should fluctuate with the set air flow.
6. Turn off the air needle valve and the air cylinder.
7. Ensure that the pressure value displayed on the system-based air high pressure gauge decreases by less than 10% within one minute.
8. Exit and set the air flow to 6 L/min.
9. Confirm that the Insufficient air supply pressure alarm and Low driving gas pressure alarm are generated as the air source pressure decreases.
10.Check that the reading of the air high pressure gauge drops to zero. The drive gas pressure low alarm will occur only when the machine is configured for air drive.

N2O: 6.4.3 N2O Cylinder Supply Test
1. Remove the N2O source hose from the gas inlet assembly. Make sure that the N2O supply is available.
2. Mount the backup cylinder full of N2O on the backup cylinder yoke.
3. Observe the reading on the N2O high pressure gauge for the entire system. Ensure that the difference between the pressure displayed on the system-based N2O high pressure gauge and the pressure displayed on the cylinder pressure gauge does not exceed 4% of the full-scale reading + 8% of the actual reading.
4. Turn on the system switch and set the ventilation mode to manual.
5. Adjust the N2O flow to 6 L/min. The O2 flow should increase to about 2 L/min accordingly (for A7) or 2 L/min (for A5).
6. Set the N2O flow to 0 and turn off the N2O cylinder.
7. Check that the pressure value displayed on the system-based N2O high pressure gauge decreases by less than 10% within one minute.
8. Set the N2O flow to 6 L/min.
9. Confirm that the Insufficient O2 supply pressure alarm is generated as the N2O source pressure decreases.
10.Check that the reading of the N2O high pressure gauge drops to zero.

items: O2 cylinder supply test.
Air cylinder supply test.
N2O cylinder supply test.

steps.title: AGSS check
steps.instructions:
6.5.1 Active AGSS Check Connect to the AGSS, connect the gas source, and check whether the float is floating between the MAX and MIN marks. If the float cannot be positioned between the MAX and MIN marks by the flow adjustment knob at the top of the AGSS, or if the float moves stickily or is damaged, disassemble or replace the float according to the following possible solutions Do not block the pressure compensation port of the AGSS during check. If the float is not floating, the possible reasons are as follows:
1. The float is sticky or stuck on the guide rod. Invert the AGSS to check whether the float can move up and down freely. If it cannot move up and down freely, clean the matching section of the float and guide rod to remove any foreign objects. If necessary, replace the float or guide rod.
2. The filter may be blocked. Remove the filter according to the following method and check whether the filter in the top cover is blocked.
1)Rotate the top cover counterclockwise to separate the top cover from the observation window, and then take out the filter.
2)Shake the removed filter to shake off the dust and impurities on the filter until a satisfactory cleaning effect.
3. The waste gas disposal system is not working or the pumping rate is lower than the normal working flow rate of the AGSS. Check whether the waste gas disposal system can reach the pumping rate range claimed by the AGSS. The claimed flow rate of the low-flow AGSS is 25 L/ min to 50 L/min, and the claimed flow rate of the high-flow AGSS is 75 L/min to 105 L/min.
Mark N/A for the flow range that doesn’t apply.

items: High-flow AGSS: pump rate meets the manufacturer’s requirement, 75–105 L/min.
Low-flow AGSS: pump rate meets the manufacturer’s requirement, 25–50 L/min.
The AGSS flow on the display status is between the MIN and MAX lines.

steps.title: Negative pressure suction: pipeline and venturi
steps.instructions:
Mark N/A for a suction type not fitted.

Pipeline: 6.6.1 Pipeline Negative Pressure Suction Test
1. Check that the suction tube between overflow protection cup, filter and collection bottle is correctly connected.
2. Connect the external negative pressure source to the negative pressure air inlet assembly of the anesthesia machine by using a negative pressure air source hose.
3. Fold the patient end of the suction tube, set the negative pressure regulator to the FULL position, and check whether the negative pressure regulator displays a value greater than 65 kPa.
4. Set the negative pressure regulator to the OFF position and check whether the pointer on the negative pressure gauge gradually returns to the zero position.
5. Set the negative pressure regulator to the REG position and turn the negative pressure adjustment knob synchronously and slowly. When the knob is turned clockwise, the pressure the pressure value displayed on the negative pressure gauge gradually decreases until it returns to zero; when the knob is turned counterclockwise, the pressure value displayed on the negative pressure gauge gradually increases until it reaches the maximum value.
6. Set the pressure regulator to the OFF position again and loosen the folded negative pressure suction pipeline.
7. Disconnect the negative pressure air source hose. If there is no reading on the negative pressure gauge or the reading value is less than 65 kPa, the possible reasons are as follows:
1)No negative pressure is output from the external negative pressure source.
2)The negative pressure suction tube is incorrectly connected.
3)The overflow protection cup, filter and collection bottle are incorrectly installed

Venturi: 6.6.2 Venturi Negative Pressure Suction Test
1. Check that the suction tube between overflow protection cup, filter and collection bottle is correctly connected.
2. Connect the external air source to the air inlet assembly of the anesthesia machine by using an air source hose.
3. Fold the patient end of the suction tube, set the negative pressure regulator to the FULL position, and check whether the negative pressure regulator displays a value greater than 50 kPa.
4. Set the negative pressure regulator to the OFF position and check whether the pointer on the negative pressure gauge gradually returns to the zero position.
5. Set the negative pressure regulator to the REG position and turn the negative pressure adjustment knob synchronously and slowly. When the knob is turned clockwise, the pressure value displayed on the negative pressure gauge gradually decreases until it returns to zero; when the knob is turned counterclockwise, the pressure value displayed on the negative pressure gauge gradually increases until it reaches the maximum value.
6. Set the pressure regulator to the OFF position again and loosen the folded negative pressure suction pipeline.
7. Disconnect the air source hose. Do not block the exhaust port of the muffler during the check. If there is no reading on the negative pressure gauge, the possible reasons are as follows:
1)No air is output from the external air source or the pressure is lower than 280 kPa.
2)The negative pressure suction tube is incorrectly connected.
3)The muffler may be blocked by dust or debris.

items: Pipeline: the negative pressure gauge shows the maximum negative pressure with the regulator at FULL.
Pipeline: the gauge returns to zero gradually with the regulator at OFF.
Pipeline: the pressure decreases gradually to zero when the knob is turned clockwise.
Pipeline: the pressure increases gradually to the maximum when the knob is turned counterclockwise.
Venturi: the negative pressure gauge shows the maximum negative pressure with the regulator at FULL.
Venturi: the gauge returns to zero gradually with the regulator at OFF.
Venturi: the pressure decreases gradually to zero when the knob is turned clockwise.
Venturi: the pressure increases gradually to the maximum when the knob is turned counterclockwise.

steps.title: Auxiliary flowmeter and high-flow O2 (HFNC)
steps.instructions:
Mark N/A for options not fitted.

6.7.2 Auxiliary O2 Supply Test
1. Provide the anesthesia machine with the O2 source.
2. Rotate the O2 needle valve on the auxiliary O2 supply panel. Turn the needle valve to its maximum setting. Ensure that the flow can be adjusted to 15 L/min and the glass tube flow indicator is at 15±1.5 L/min.
3. Close the O2 needle valve on the auxiliary O2 supply panel and ensure that the auxiliary flowmeter is turned off and the glass tube float is at the bottom.
6.7.3 Auxiliary O2/Air Test
1. Provide the anesthesia machine with the O2 source and air source.
2. Click the auxiliary flowmeter switch and confirm that the auxiliary flowmeter is started.
3. After the auxiliary flowmeter is started, the initial flow value is 0, the initial O2 concentration value is 100% and the glass tube float should be at the bottom.
4. Set the O2 concentration to 100% and confirm the maximum flow can be adjusted to 15 L/min and the flow indication of the glass tube is 15 L/min±1.5 L/min.
5. Adjust the O2 concentration to 21% and confirm the maximum flow can be adjusted to 15 L/min and the flow indication of the glass tube is 15 L/min±1.5 L/min.
6. Press the auxiliary flowmeter switch, and ensure that the auxiliary flowmeter is turned off and the glass tube float is at the bottom

6.7.4 HFNC Test
1. Provide the anesthesia machine with the O2 source and air source.
2. Click the high flow O2 supply switch and confirm that high flow O2 supply is enabled.
3. After the auxiliary flowmeter is started, the initial flow value is 0, the initial O2 concentration value is 100% and the glass tube float should be at the bottom.
4. Set the O2 concentration to 100% and confirm the maximum flow can be adjusted to 60 L/min and the flow indication of the glass tube is around 60 L/min (the deviation does not exceed 10 L/min).
5. Press and hold the HFNC switch for a few seconds, release it and ensure that HFNC is disabled and the glass tube float is at the bottom

items: Aux flowmeter: initial flow is 0, initial O2 concentration is 100% and the glass tube float is at the bottom.
Aux flowmeter at 100% O2: flow adjusts to a maximum of 15 L/min and the glass tube reads 15±1.5 L/min.
Aux flowmeter at 21% O2: flow adjusts to a maximum of 15 L/min and the glass tube reads 15±2 L/min.
Aux flowmeter: pressing and holding the switch turns it off and the float returns to the bottom.
HFNC: high-flow O2 is disabled and the glass tube float is at the bottom.
HFNC at 100% O2: flow adjusts to a maximum of 60 L/min and the glass tube reads about 60 L/min (within 10 L/min).
HFNC: pressing and holding the switch disables high-flow O2 and the float returns to the bottom.

steps.title: Semi-electronic flowmeter
steps.instructions:
Mindray’s A5/A7 PM checklist says the A6 and A7 don’t have this part: mark N/A if it isn’t fitted.

6.8.1 Semi-Electronic Flowmeter Test Slowly rotate all gas flow switches. Do not turn the control knob over the maximum or minimum values on the flowmeter, as this may damage the control valve and cause a loss of control.  If N2O is present and flowing through the system during this test, use a safe and approved method to collect and dispose of it.  Improper gas mixtures can cause patient injury. The O2/N2O proportioning system should not be used if it does not deliver the correct proportion of O2 and N2O. Flow control system test procedure:
1. Connect the pipeline gas supply or slowly open the cylinder valve.
2. Turn all flow control knobs on the flowmeter clockwise to the closed position.
3. Turn on the system switch.
4. If the battery is low, connect the AC power supply. Do not use the system if any other ventilator alarms are active.
5. Adjust the flow control knobs to set the flow rate to the middle of the measurement range.
6. O2-N2O system test (with the N2O flow increased):
1)Turn the O2 and N2O flow control knobs clockwise to set both O2 and N2O flows to maximum.
2)Adjust only the N2O flow control knob.
3)Gradually increase the N2O flow according to the values in the table below, and observe the O2 flow value at each step. Ensure that the flow values are not less than the corresponding values in the table for each step.
4)If the N2O flow is over-adjusted, turn the O2 flow clockwise until the N2O flow is reduced to the previously set value before continuing the test.
8. Shut off the N2O pipeline supply or close the N2O cylinder. Turn the O2 and N2O flow knobs counterclockwise to ensure that there is no residual gas in the N2O branch and the N2O branch pressure gauge returns to zero. Then turn the O2 and N2O flow knobs clockwise to ensure that the O2 and N2O flows are both adjusted to the minimum.
9. Shut off the O2 pipeline supply or close the O2 cylinder. When the O2 supply is cut off, the O2 supply pressure will decrease, which will trigger an alarm for insufficient O2 supply pressure and low driving gas pressure.

items: N2O 0.9 L/min: O2 is at least 0.3 L/min.
N2O 1.5 L/min: O2 is at least 0.5 L/min.
N2O 3 L/min: O2 is at least 1 L/min.
N2O 6 L/min: O2 is at least 2 L/min.

steps.title: EFCS accuracy: O2 and balance gas
steps.instructions:
Switch the system to the manual mode, exit the standby mode, and expose the bag arm port to ambient air. Adjust the fresh gas flow according to the table below and observe whether the flow displayed on the on-screen electronic flowmeter meets the acceptance criteria.

O2 electronic flowmeter: Balance gas setting = None
Start a case in Manual mode.
Set the O2 flows to 0.2, 1, 10 and 15L.
Enter the Service menu > Data Monitors > FCS.
Confirm O2 flow readings.

Balance gas flowmeter: Set to 21% O2 (Air)
Start a case in Manual mode.
Set the Air flow to 0.2, 1, 10 and 15L.
Enter the Service menu > Data Monitors > FCS.
Confirm Balance Limb Flow readings.

items: O2 set to 0.2 L/min: reads 0.15–0.25 L/min.
O2 set to 1 L/min: reads 0.95–1.05 L/min.
O2 set to 10 L/min: reads 9.5–10.5 L/min.
O2 set to 15 L/min: reads 14.25–15.75 L/min.
Balance gas set to 15 L/min: reads 14.25–15.75 L/min.
Balance gas set to 10 L/min: reads 9.5–10.5 L/min.
Balance gas set to 1 L/min: reads 0.95–1.05 L/min.
Balance gas set to 0.2 L/min: reads 0.15–0.25 L/min.

steps.title: Vaporizers and internal AG module
steps.instructions:
Mark N/A for a vaporizer position or AG module not fitted.

6.9.1 Vaporizer Self-lock Test
1. Connect the vaporizer to the vaporizer support and lock it.
2. Verify that the vaporizer is securely attached and does not shake or detach.
3. Remove the vaporizer and connect it to the other vaporizer support.
4. Verify that the vaporizer is securely attached and does not shake or detach
6.9.2 Vaporizer Interlock Test
1. Connect two vaporizers to the vaporizer support and lock them in proper positions.
2. Rotate the dial of either vaporizer to 3%.
3. Make sure that the dial of the other vaporizer cannot be rotated.
4. Set the dials of both vaporizers to 0.
5. Rotate the dial of the other vaporizer to 3%.
6. Make sure that the dial of the first vaporizer cannot be rotated.
7. Rotate the dials of both vaporizers to 0 or T and remove both vaporizers.
8. Make sure that the locking spring is intact.
9. Reconnect both vaporizers to the vaporizer support

6.9.3 vaporizer Accuracy Test
1. Set the APL valve to SP.
2. Turn the Manual/Auto switch to the Manual position.
3. Connect the inspiratory port to the expiratory port by using a breathing tube. Block the manual arm port by using a manual leather bag.
4. Connect the sampling line of the AG module to the suction port of the anesthesia machine, and connect the exhaust port of the AG module to the sample gas return port, as shown in the figure (Service Manual chapter 6.9.3)
5. Verify that the purification system is connected to the wall and the float is between the MIN line and the MAX line.
6. Mount the vaporizer and add anesthetic (if necessary)
7. Power on the anesthesia machine, exit the standby mode and run the anesthesia machine in manual mode. Observe the displayed value of the AG module on anesthesia machine.
8. Test the accuracy of the vaporizer according to instructions of the manufacturer.
9. Test vaporizers in turn.

6.9.4 Vaporizer Leakage Test
1. Turn the Manual/Auto switch to the Manual position.
2. Turn the APL valve to the SP position.
3. Connect the manual leather bag to the manual arm port.
4. Connect the Y-shaped head in the respiratory circuit to the leakage test end and connect the other two ends to the expiratory end and inspiratory end of the circuit.
Note: If the AG module is configured, the sampling tube and exhaust tube of the AG module must be connected at the same time or neither of tubes is not connected. When the tubes are not connected, the Y-piece sampling port must be blocked.
5. Mount and lock the vaporizer onto the vaporizer support. (The vaporizer must be set to at least 1%.)
6. Set the fresh air flow to 0.2 L/min.
7. Set the APL valve to 70 cmH2O.
8. Press the fast oxygenation button to increase the value of the airway pressure gauge to about 30 cmH2O.
9. Release the fast oxygenation button. Observe the airway pressure gauge and make sure that the reading of the pressure gauge does not drop.
10.Turn off the vaporizer

items: Vaporizer 1 is securely attached and doesn’t shake or detach.
Vaporizer 2 is securely attached and doesn’t shake or detach.
Vaporizer 1 dial can’t be rotated when vaporizer 2 is dialled to 3%.
Vaporizer 2 dial can’t be rotated when vaporizer 1 is dialled to 3%.
AG module with vaporizer at 0%: reads below 0.05%.
AG module at 0.2%: reads 0–0.45%.
AG module at 1%: reads 0.75–1.25%.
AG module at 3%: reads 2.55–3.45%.
AG module at 5%: reads 4.25–5.75%.
AG module at 8%: reads 6.8–9.2%.
Internal AG module extraction flow is stable at 150±5 mL/min.
Vaporizer 1 passes the leakage test (dial at least 1%, fresh gas 0.2 L/min, APL 70, flush to about 30 cmH2O: the pressure doesn’t drop).
Vaporizer 2 passes the leakage test (same settings).

steps.title: Fresh gas special circuits: O2 flush, ACGO and high-pressure O2
steps.instructions:
O2 flush: 6.10.1 Quick O2 Supply Test
1. Connect the O2 pipeline source or open the O2 backup cylinder.
2. Turn the Manual/Auto switch to the Manual position.
3. Keep the anesthesia machine in standby mode.
4. Connect the Y-shaped head in the respiratory circuit to the leakage test end and connect the other two ends to the expiratory end and inspiratory end of the circuit.
5. Connect a 3 L or 1 L leather bag to the manual arm interface.
6. Set ACGO to OFF.
7. Adjust the APL valve to 70 cmH2O.
8. Continuously press the fast oxygenation button and measure the time used to fully fill the leather bag.
9. Repeat the operation more than twice.
10.Check that the time used to fill the leather bag is within the following range:  3 L leather bag: 3s to 6s.  1 L leather bag: 1s to 3s.

ACGO: 6.10.2 Mechanical ACGO Function Test
1. Set the fresh air flow to 1 L/min, the mode to VCV and the patient type to Adult and retain default values of other parameters. Connect the patient pipeline to the simulated lung and ventilate the equipment for three to five cycles normally.
2. Turn the ACGO switch to the ACGO mode and confirm that "VCV" in the display area in system ventilation mode is replaced with "ACGO".
3. Block the ACGO outlet and observe the screen until the airway pressure waveform on the screen rises obviously.
4. Turn the ACGO switch to another mode than the ACGO mode and verify that the system switches to the VCV mode and the ventilation is normal.

High-pressure O2 output: 6.11.1 High Pressure O2 Output Test When the O2 inlet is connected to O2, press the high-pressure O2 output check valve by using your fingers and confirm that a high-pressure gas is output. Release the high-pressure O2 inlet check valve and ensure that no gas is output from the highpressure O2 inlet

items: O2 flush (APL 70 cmH2O, ACGO off): the 3 L bag fills in 3–6 s, or the 1 L bag in 1–3 s.
ACGO (fresh gas 1 L/min, VCV adult): the PAW waveform clearly rises when the ACGO outlet is blocked.
ACGO: "VCV" in the ventilation mode area is replaced with "ACGO" in ACGO mode.
ACGO: switching out of ACGO returns the system to VCV and ventilation is normal.
ACGO: the airway pressure gauge rises above 30 cmH2O within one minute in ACGO mode.
The unit passes the high-pressure O2 output test.

steps.title: Breathing circuit tests
steps.instructions:
O2 concentration: 6.12.1 O2 Concentration Test
Note: When performing this test in the EFCS state, air must be set as the balance gas and the direct flow control mode must be set. The system must be connected to O2 and the air supplies.
1. Set ventilator control parameters as follows:
Patient Size = Adult
Ventilation Mode = VCV
Vt = 1000
Rate = 10
I:E = 1:2
Tp = Off
PEEP = Off
Plimit = 100
2. Adjust the O2 and air flow to 3 L/min. Wait for one minute until the O2 concentration is stable. The concentration displayed on the screen is 60±3%. Verify that the concentration for external standard equipment is 60±3%.
3. Turn off all flow regulators.

APL valve: 6.12.2 APL Valve Test
1. Turn the Manual/Auto switch to the Manual position.
2. Connect the manual leather bag to the manual arm port.
3. Connect the Y-shaped head in the breathing circuit to the leakage test port.
4. Turn the APL valve control knob to 30 cmH2O.
5. Press the quick oxygenation button to inflate the manual leather bag.
6. Ensure that the value displayed on the air pressure gauge ranges from 20 cmH2O to 40 cmH2O.
7. Pull up the APL valve, observe the reading of the airway pressure gauge and confirm that the pressure value can immediately drop to 0±2 cmH2O.
8. Turn the APL valve control knob to the SP (minimum) position.
9. Set the O2 flow rate to 3 L/min. Close other gases.
10.Ensure that the value displayed on the air pressure gauge is smaller than 5 cmH2O.
11.Push the quick oxygenation button continuously. Ensure that the value displayed on the air pressure gauge does not exceed 10 cmH2O.
12.Release the quick oxygenation button and turn the O2 flow control knob to the minimum position. Ensure that the value displayed on the air pressure gauge does not decrease below 0 cmH2O

Patient circuit heating: 6.12.4 Patient Circuit Heating Function Check Ensure that the system adopts AC power supply and is in standby mode and the patient circuit remains in place. Make the heating module work for more than 10 minutes. On the following interface, access the diagnosis data interface and select
Setup>>Service>>Data Monitors>>Monitoring Board. Observe the actual temperature values displayed by heater temperature sensor 1 and heater temperature sensor 2, which should be in the range of 50°C to 70°C.

Sample gas return: 6.12.5 Test on the Sample Gas Return Function
Checking the Sample Gas Exhaust Port Press the spring above the snap hook on the sample gas exhaust port and verify that the snap hook supports self-locking. In this state, the quick connector can be normally connected.
Leakage Test in Sample Gas Return Mode Connect a quick connector to the sample gas return port at one end of the machine when the rubber hose at the other end is blocked. Set the system to perform an automatic leakage test. Follow instructions on the screen for the test and verify that the leakage test is passed.
Tidal Volume Test in Sample Gas Return Mode When a module is installed in the module rack and the module is warmed up, connect the exhaust port of the AG module to the rubber hose of the quick connector and connect the quick connector to the sample gas return port. Set the O2 flow to about 1 L/min and set system parameters as follows:
Vt = 500
Rate = 8
Tp = 30
I:E = 1:2
PEEP = 5 Ventilate the connected simulated lung. After running for 10 waveforms in ventilation mode, ensure that the displayed Vt value is in the range 455-545 mL.

items: O2 concentration (O2 and air 3 L/min each, VCV Vt 1000 mL): the external analyser reads 60 ±3% (57–63%).
APL valve at 30 cmH2O: the PAW gauge reads 20–40 cmH2O.
APL valve pulled: the pressure immediately drops to 0±2 cmH2O.
APL valve at SP (minimum): the PAW gauge reads below 5 cmH2O.
With O2 flush held: the PAW gauge doesn’t exceed 10 cmH2O.
After releasing O2 flush: the PAW gauge doesn’t drop below 0 cmH2O.
Heater temperature sensors 1 and 2 read 50–70 °C after more than 10 minutes heating.
The sample gas exhaust port snap hook self-locks.
The sample gas return leak test passes.
Sample gas return (Vt set 500 mL, rate 8, PEEP 5, O2 about 1 L/min): displayed Vt is 500 mL ±45 mL (455–545 mL).

steps.title: Alarm tests
steps.instructions:
Power failure: 6.13 Alarm Test
6.13.1 Power Failure Alarm Test
1. Turn the system switch to the ON position.
2. Disconnect the AC power supply.
3. Ensure that the AC power indicator is off. An audible alarm should be reported and the following message should be displayed on the main screen: Battery in Use.
4. Reconnect the AC power supply.
5. Ensure that an audible alarm is reported and the AC power indicator is on. The prompt message Battery in Use should not be displayed on the main screen.
6. Set the system switch to the OFF position.

Ventilator alarms: 6.13.4 Ventilator Alarm Tests
Setup
1. Ensure that the pressures of O2, N2O, and air are within the specified range.
2. Power on the anesthesia system.
3. Carry out the startup test as instructed by the system. Ensure that the test is successfully completed.
4. Connect the breathing circuit and bag. For testing purposes, always use a reusable breathing circuit.
5. Connect the adult test lung to the Y-connector of the breathing circuit.
6. Set O2 flow rate to 2 L/min. Disable the N2O and air supply.
7. Set the respiratory parameters as follows:
Patient Size = Adult
Ventilation Mode = VCV
Vt = 500
Rate = 10
I:E = 1:2
Tpause = Off
PEEP = Off
Plimit = 40
8. Start ventilation.
FiO2 Too Low Alarm Test
1. Set the "FiO2 Too Low" alarm limit to 50%.
2. Set the air flow rate to 5 L/min.
3. Disable the O2 supply.
4. Ensure that the "FiO2 Too Low" alarm signal appears in three ventilation cycles:  The screen displays FiO2 Too Low alarm information.  An alarm tone sounds.
5. Set the "FiO2 Too Low" alarm limit to 18%.
6. Ensure that the alarm signal stops.
FiO2 Too High Alarm Test
1. Set the "FiO2 Too High" alarm limit to 50%.
2. Set the O2 flow rate to 5 L/min.
3. Disable the air supply.
4. Ensure that the "FiO2 Too High" alarm signal appears:  The screen displays FiO2 Too High alarm information.  An alarm tone sounds.
5. Set the "FiO2 Too High" alarm limit to the maximum value.
6. Ensure that the alarm signal stops.

Paw Pressure Alarm Test
1. Set the Peak low alarm limit to the minimum value.
2. Set the Peak high alarm limit to about 5-8 cmH2O below the peak pressure shown on the screen.
3. Ensure that the following pressure alarm appears:
1)The screen displays Paw Too High alarm information.
2)An alarm tone sounds.
3)When the pressure reaches the high alarm limit, stop inspiratory and start expiratory.
4. Set the Peak high alarm limit to 65 (cmH2O).
5. Ensure that the alarm signal stops.
6. Set the Peak low alarm limit to 50 (cmH2O).
7. Ensure that the following pressure alarm appears:
1)The screen displays Paw Too Low alarm information.
2)An alarm tone sounds.
8. Set the "Paw Too Low" alarm limit to 1 (cmH2O).
9. Ensure that the alarm signal stops.
Minute Ventilation Alarm Test
1. Set the MV high alarm limit and low alarm limit to the maximum values.
2. Ensure that the following alarm appears:  The screen displays MV Too Low alarm information.  An alarm tone sounds.
3. Set the MV low alarm limit to the minimum value.
4. Ensure that the alarm signal stops.
5. Set the MV high alarm limit to the minimum value.
6. Ensure that the following alarm appears:  The screen displays MV Too High alarm information.  An alarm tone sounds.
7. Set the MV high alarm limit to the maximum value.
8. Ensure that the alarm signal stops.

Apnea Alarm Test
1. Turn the Manual/Auto switch to Manual mode, rotate the APL valve to the 30 cmH2O position, and connect the Y-shaped head in the breathing circuit to the leakage test port.
2. Connect the manual arm to the bag, press the quick O2 supply key to fill the bag with gas, and gently squeeze the bag by hand to generate a breathing waveform.
3. Remove the bag, and make the connecting port face the atmosphere directly for at least 30s to ensure that the Apnea alarm is triggered.
4. Connect the bag and create a breathing waveform to ensure that the Apnea alarm disappears.
Sustained Airway Pressure Alarm Test
1. Connect the bag to the bag port.
2. Set the O2 flow rate to 0.2 L/min.
3. Rotate the APL valve control knob and set the value to 30 cmH2O.
4. Turn the Manual/Auto switch to Manual mode.
5. Press the O2 flush button for about 20s. Ensure that the "Sustained Airway Pressure" alarm appears.

items: "Respiratory Circuit Not Installed" alarm occurs when the patient circuit is removed.
"CO2 Absorber Canister Not Locked" alarm occurs when the canister handle is open.
Power failure: "Battery in Use" is displayed and the audible alarm works.
"FiO2 Too Low" (limit set to 50%, air 5 L/min, O2 off) appears and the alarm is audible.
"FiO2 Too High" (limit set to 50%, O2 5 L/min, air off) appears and the alarm is audible.
"Paw Too High" (high limit 5–8 cmH2O below the peak) appears and the alarm is audible.
"Paw Too Low" (low limit set to 50 cmH2O) appears and the alarm is audible.
"MV Too Low" (both MV limits at maximum) appears and the alarm is audible.
"MV Too High" (MV high limit at minimum) appears and the alarm is audible.
Apnea alarm occurs (bag port open to air for at least 30 s).
"Sustained Airway Pressure" alarm occurs (O2 0.2 L/min, APL 30 cmH2O, O2 flush held about 20 s).
Each alert message and sound clears after the limit is reset.

steps.title: Ventilation performance: manual, VCV and PCV
steps.instructions:
Manual: 6.14 System Ventilation Performance Test
6.14.1 Manual Mode Ventilation Test
1. Set the Auto/Manual switch to the Manual position. Press the screen to switch the system to the manual mode.
2. Set the APL valve value to 30 cmH2O. Push the O2 Flush button to fill the breathing bag.
3. Set the flow rate to 1 L/min.
4. Squeeze the bag every 3s.
5. Ensure that the expansion and contraction of the test lung are normal.
6. Ensure that the airway pressure waveforms and all values are displayed on the screen during contraction of the bag.
7. Stop squeezing the bag and adjust the APL valve to the SP position

VCV adult: 6.14.2 VCV Adult Ventilation Mode Test
1. Connect the breathing circuit and bag. For testing purposes, always use a reusable breathing circuit.
2. Connect the adult test lung to the Y-connector of the breathing circuit.
3. Connect a ventilation test device between the expiratory end and the breathing tube.
4. Set O2 flow rate to 2 L/min. Disable the N2O and air supply.
5. Set the Auto/Manual switch to the Auto position.
6. Set the respiratory parameters as follows:
Patient Size = Adult
Ventilation Mode = VCV
Vt = 500
Rate = 10
I:E = 1:2
Tpause = Off
PEEP = Off
Plimit = 40
7. Start ventilation.
8. Ensure that the screen displays the pressure waveform, breathing volume, mean pressure or plateau pressure, breathing rate and minute volume normally.
9. Ensure that the tidal volume displayed by the anesthesia machine in 1 minute after the start of ventilation is within 7% (±35 mL) of the value displayed on the ventilation test device.
10.Ensure that the tidal volume displayed by the anesthesia machine in 1 minute after the start of ventilation is within 7% (±35 mL) of the preset value.

PCV adult: 6.14.4 PCV Adult Ventilation Mode Test
1. Connect the breathing circuit and bag. For testing purposes, always use a reusable breathing circuit.
2. Connect the adult test lung to the Y-connector of the breathing circuit.
3. Connect a ventilation test device between the expiratory end and the breathing tube.
4. Set O2 flow rate to 3 L/min. Disable the N2O and air supply.
5. Set the respiratory parameters as follows:
Patient Size = Adult
Ventilation Mode = PCV
VtG = Off
Pinsp = 15
Rate = 8
I:E = 1:2
Tslope = 0.2
PEEP = Off
6. Start ventilation.
7. Ensure that the peak pressure value displayed by the screen is within ±2 cmH2O of the preset
Pinsp value.
8. Ensure that the screen displays the pressure waveform, breathing volume, breathing rate and minute volume normally.
9. Ensure that the peak value obtained by the ventilation test device within 5 breathing cycles since the start of ventilation reaches 15±2 cmH2O

VCV child: 6.14.3 VCV Child Ventilation Mode Test
1. Connect the breathing circuit and bag. For testing purposes, always use a reusable breathing circuit.
2. Connect the adult test lung to the Y-connector of the breathing circuit. Limit the volume in the test lung to provide sufficient airway pressure to satisfy the Low Peak Pressure alarm. Or set the peak pressure alarm limit to a lower value to prevent the alarm when using an adult test lung.
3. Connect a ventilation test device between the expiratory end and the breathing tube.
4. Set O2 flow rate to 2 L/min. Set the N2O and air flow rates to the minimum values.
5. Set the respiratory parameters as follows:
Patient Size = Child
Ventilation Mode = VCV
Vt = 300 (the ±21 mL tolerance is 7% of 300 mL, as in Mindray’s PM checklist)
Rate = 15
I:E = 1:2
Tpause = 10
PEEP = Off
Plimit = 40
6. Start the ventilation.
7. Ensure that the screen displays the pressure waveform, breathing volume, mean pressure or plateau pressure, breathing rate and minute volume normally.
8. Ensure that the tidal volume displayed by the anesthesia machine in 1 minute after the start of ventilation is within 7% (±21 mL) of the value displayed on the ventilation test device
9. Ensure that the tidal volume displayed by the anesthesia machine in 1 minute after the start of ventilation is about 7% (±21 mL) of the preset value

items: Manual (APL 30 cmH2O, 1 L/min, squeeze every 3 s): the test lung inflates and deflates.
Manual: the PAW waveform and all values appear during bag compression.
VCV adult (Vt 500 mL, rate 10, I:E 1:2, Plimit 40, O2 2 L/min): pressure waveform, volume, mean or plateau pressure, rate and minute volume are displayed.
VCV adult: Vt on the machine is within 7% (±35 mL) of the ventilation tester reading.
VCV adult: Vt on the machine is 500 mL ±35 mL (465–535 mL).
PCV adult (Pinsp 15 cmH2O, rate 8, I:E 1:2, PEEP off, O2 3 L/min): displayed peak pressure is 15 ±2 cmH2O (13–17 cmH2O).
PCV adult: pressure waveform, volume, rate and minute volume are displayed.
PCV adult: the ventilation tester peak reaches 15 ±2 cmH2O (13–17 cmH2O) within the first five breaths.
VCV child (Vt 300 mL, rate 15, I:E 1:2, Plimit 40, O2 2 L/min): pressure waveform, volume, mean or plateau pressure, rate and minute volume are displayed.
VCV child: Vt on the machine is within 7% (±21 mL) of the ventilation tester reading.
VCV child: Vt on the machine is 300 mL ±21 mL (279–321 mL).

steps.title: Sensors: pressure and flow accuracy, zero point
steps.instructions:
Pressure sensor accuracy: To check the measurement accuracy of pressure sensors, perform the following operations:
1. Make the machine enter the standby mode, remove the patient circuit, and mount the pressure calibration test fixture to the circuit adapter block in place.
2. Connect the syringe and the pressure sampling port of the pressure test equipment by using a three-way silicon tube.
3. Set the calibration device as described below. To set the VT-Plus, perform the following operations: a. Pressure settings: Press the PRESSURE button on the front calibration control panel. Select Range and then set it to Low Press.
4. Choose Setup > Service > Data Monitors > VCM and find the actual airway pressure values.
5. Adjust the pressure by using the syringe so that the pressure test equipment displays (5±1) cmH2O, (20±1) cmH2O, (50±1) cmH2O, (70±2) cmH2O, and (90±2) cmH2O in sequence. 6. Ensure that the deviation between the measured value of the PAW sensor displayed on the machine and that of the pressure test equipment does not exceed 1 cmH2O or 2% of the measured value of the calibration device, whichever is greater. Otherwise, perform pressure calibration again.

Flow sensor accuracy: To check the measurement accuracy of flow sensors, perform the following operations:
1. Remove the water collection cup.
2. Use a pipe to connect the inspiratory port and expiratory port of the anesthesia machine, as shown in the following figure
3. Choose Setup > Service > Diagnostic Tests > Valves to access the flow test screen.
4. Set Safety Valve to On.
5. Set PEEP Valve Pressure to 100 cmH2O, and Auto/Manual Valve to Auto.
6. Set Insp Valve Flow to the following values: 3L/min, 10L/min, 20L/min, 30L/min, and 60L/min.
7. Check the values displayed on the inspiratory flow sensor and expiratory flow sensor. The deviations between these values and the measured values of the flow sensors on the anesthesia machine do not exceed 1 L/min or 5% of the measured values of the flow sensors on the anesthesia machine, whichever is greater. Otherwise, perform flow calibration again.
8. After calibration is completed, reinstall the water collection cup.

Zero point (enter the current zero point of each sensor below): To check the sensor zero point, perform the following operations:
1. Disconnect the tubes from the inspiratory and expiratory ports.
2. Ensure that the system is in standby mode.
3. Choose Setup > Service > Data Monitors > Zero Sensors to access the zero display screen. The second column is the zero point of the current sensor and the third column is the zero point in case of factory calibration. The following table lists the normal range of the zero point of some pressure and flow sensors. If the current zero point exceeds the specified normal range and the actual value is greater than 1, calibrate the zero point again. If the actual value is less than 1 and the zero point of the PAW sensor, PEEP sensor, or inspiratory/expiratory flow sensor is beyond the range, replace the VCM. If the zero point of the balance gas flow sensor, O2 flow sensor, or total flow sensor is beyond the range, replace the flow sensor or its interface board.

items: PAW sensor at 5 cmH2O: reads 4–6 cmH2O.
PAW sensor at 20 cmH2O: reads 19–21 cmH2O.
PAW sensor at 50 cmH2O: reads 49–51 cmH2O.
PAW sensor at 70 cmH2O: reads 68–72 cmH2O.
PAW sensor at 90 cmH2O: reads 88–92 cmH2O.
Flow sensors at 3 L/min: read 2–4 L/min.
Flow sensors at 10 L/min: read 9–11 L/min.
Flow sensors at 20 L/min: read 19–21 L/min.
Flow sensors at 30 L/min: read 28.5–31.5 L/min.
Flow sensors at 60 L/min: read 57–63 L/min.
